name: Fairchild Micrologic Type F flip-flop
summary: Fairchild's Micrologic Type F flip-flop, offered in March 1961 at $120 each in evaluation lots, was among the first integrated circuits anyone could buy.
description: Fairchild Micrologic Type F integrated flip-flop, 1961 introductory evaluation product; isolation process of earliest sold samples unconfirmed.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

impact.note: One early chip product sold in small evaluation lots, an advance on discrete circuits, followed by the Micrologic family; implies tier 3, two below reviewed tier 1.

why: Fairchild sought to turn its planar integrated-circuit work into products for computer and control-logic designers.

market.note: The contemporaneous report states evaluation quantities were being sold.

evidence.supports: Says the Fairchild Micrologic flip-flop was being sold in evaluation quantities on 29 March 1961.

date.label: March 1961
date.basis: Introduced in March and contemporary 29/31 March reports identify paid evaluation sales and an offer.

events.statement: The Micrologic flip-flop was being sold in evaluation quantities in March 1961; the introductory unit price was $120.
events.scope: Micrologic Type F flip-flop; evaluation quantities
events.caveats: The first day of the offer and the early samples isolation process are unconfirmed; five other elements were not yet generally available according to the March 31 report. Actual purchaser geography is not established by the inspected sources.

evidence.supports: Says the Fairchild Micrologic flip-flop was being sold in evaluation quantities on 29 March 1961.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 76, PDF p. 78, New on the Market
evidence.supports: Says first Micrologic flip-flop now available, introductory price $120, while other elements were to follow.
Fairchild states the flip-flop was first made available in March and describes it as commercially available.

evidence.locator: PDF p. 19, March 1961 Micrologic entry and Type F identifier
evidence.supports: Identifies the first March 1961 Micrologic flip-flop as Type F; does not identify the isolation or mask of the earliest sold die.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest defensible dated record of this scoped referent in the retained evidence; later community entry is recorded separately. Introduced in March and contemporary 29/31 March reports identify paid evaluation sales and an offer. The first day of the offer and the early samples isolation process are unconfirmed; five other elements were not yet generally available according to the March 31 report. Actual purchaser geography is not established by the inspected sources. This is the earliest supported record currently established here, not certification of absolute priority.

community_entry.rationale: March 1961 evaluation sales directly document availability to industrial customers; the 1960 physical-isolation prototype is distinct.
community_entry.caveats: The isolation of the earliest sold units is not securely established; this is not a claim about the first use of integrated circuits generally.

caveats: March 1961 applies to first reported commercial evaluation offer, not to every Micrologic family part or later junction-isolated production die. The earliest sold die and its isolation are not established.

links.statement: The physically isolated 1960 Micrologic sample was a development antecedent of the Type F flip-flop made available in March 1961; this does not identify that particular prototype die or its isolation as the earliest sold configuration.
links.alternatives: Diffused-isolation version was developed later in 1960.
links.caveats: The accounts distinguish physical-isolation development and later diffused-isolation work; they do not identify the exact earliest sold die or establish exclusive necessity.
links.timing: Prototype May 1960 preceded evaluation sales in March 1961.

evidence.supports: Documents first working physically isolated Micrologic flip-flop in May 1960 and distinguishes later versions.
